barrow-in-furness.snapshot: Barrow-in-Furness is a Cumbrian shipbuilding town where full fibre is going in and a steady run of telecoms and CCTV work follows. We kit both sides of that trade. Build contractors and structured-cabling firms running crews across the town hold trade accounts for branded teamwear, while sole-trader broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account at all, the same lead polo, hi-vis and softshell either way.
barrow-in-furness.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Barrow and Furness
s1loc: Barrow-in-Furness has had its full-fibre build pushed hard. Openreach has finished the main part of its FTTP build across the Barrow exchange, while Fibrus is delivering the publicly funded Connecting Cumbria and Project Gigabit rollout right across the Furness peninsula, reaching Barrow, Dalton-in-Furness, Ulverston and Millom. Virgin Media holds its long-standing cable network across the town on top. Engineers work the streets and cabinets through Hindpool, Ormsgill, Hawcoat, Newbarns, Roose and out onto Walney Island, so there is a constant flow of poling, ducting and customer-premises work across the town.

Alongside the network build sits a heavy commercial scene anchored by BAE Systems at the shipyard, with Siemens, Kimberly-Clark and a deep sub-contractor base around the submarine programmes. Structured-cabling and CCTV firms wire offices, units and yards in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre across Premier Business Park on Ferry Beach Road, Channelside Business Park and the Devonshire Dock area, plus the Hindpool retail parks and the campuses of Furness College and the University of Cumbria. It is steady data-cabling, access-control and camera work for businesses right across Barrow.
